A 2019 study published through the University of Pretoria found that drivers are rarely tested for drugs and called for the law to spell out drug testing. The 2024 Act amends the road traffic law to add THC driving offences and limits, and, once it starts, makes using cannabis in a vehicle on a public road an offence with a fine of up to R2,000.
driving.citation: Lienberg et al., Drugged driving in South Africa, 2019 (research); Cannabis for Private Purposes Act 7 of 2024 s. 4 and Schedule

record-relief.short: Expungement is in the 2024 law, which has not started
record-relief.detail: The 2024 Act provides for expunging old convictions for using or possessing cannabis, and some dealing convictions that rested on a legal presumption. Some are to be wiped automatically; otherwise a person can apply in writing to the Director-General of Justice. The draft regulations say the Criminal Record Centre must confirm the expungement within 21 working days. None of this applies until the Act starts.
record-relief.citation: Cannabis for Private Purposes Act 7 of 2024 s. 5; Adams & Adams on the draft regulations (law firm)

border.short: No. Cannabis is a prohibited import
border.detail: Customs guidance from the South African Revenue Service lists narcotic and psychotropic substances, including cannabis, among the goods that are illegal to bring into South Africa. The private-use rules stop at the border.
border.citation: SAinfo traveller's customs guide, from SARS guidance (reviewed 2015)

experiment.text: The draft regulations go into detail on moving cannabis. They propose a limit of 750 grams per person a day in transit, including cannabis still on the plant, kept out of sight, preferably in the boot. Drivers would have to tell passengers it is on board before they get in. Public comment closed on March 5, 2026, and in August 2026 the rules were reported as set to be finalised soon.

differences.title: What is different about South Africa
points: A court, not Parliament, opened the door. The 2018 Prince ruling rests on the constitutional right to privacy.
Private means more than home. The court said the right to privacy reaches beyond the boundaries of a home.
The law written to follow the ruling was signed in May 2024, but it starts only when the President proclaims it, and it had not by October 2026.
Until the rules start there is no legal amount. Police weigh the quantity and the circumstances, and a court decides whether it was for dealing.
There is no legal market. Selling stays a crime, and shops calling themselves dispensaries are unlicensed.
Once the 2024 Act starts, using cannabis around children or adults who object, or where the smoke drifts into a neighbour's window, is an offence.
Drug-driving law has no THC limit yet, and a 2019 study found drivers are rarely tested for drugs.

JM.name: Jamaica
JM.summary: Ganja is still illegal for recreational use, but since April 15, 2015 having two ounces or less is a ticket, not a crime. Households may grow five plants, Rastafarians may use it as a sacrament, and licensed herb houses sell it to people with a medical recommendation.
JM.note: Jamaican law calls cannabis ganja. Amounts are in Jamaican dollars.

adult-use.short: Decriminalised, not legal
adult-use.detail: Since the Dangerous Drugs (Amendment) Act 2015 took effect on April 15, 2015, police cannot arrest, charge or try anyone for having two ounces or less, and it leaves no criminal record. They can issue a J$500 ticket. Smoking at a private home is treated the same way. Smoking in public, or within five metres of a public place, is banned like cigarette smoking and also earns a J$500 ticket. Use is lawful with a medical recommendation, as a Rastafarian sacrament, at licensed venues and at declared exempt events.
adult-use.citation: Ministry of Justice, Fact sheet on the Dangerous Drugs (Amendment) Act 2015

medical.short: Yes, on a medical recommendation
medical.detail: Possession is exempt when a registered doctor, or another health practitioner approved by the Minister of Health, recommends or prescribes it. The Cannabis Licensing Authority licenses growing, processing and retail. Under the law, visitors such as tourists can apply for a permit to buy and possess up to two ounces at a time for medical use, by showing a recommendation from a practitioner at home or signing a voluntary declaration; the Ministry of Justice fact sheet says the Ministry of Health issues it for a fee. In April 2026 the authority launched fee-free special permits to bring traditional small growers into the licensed industry.
medical.citation: Ministry of Justice fact sheet (2015); Jamaica Information Service, Apr 17 2026

buying.short: Licensed herb houses, with a recommendation
buying.detail: Licensed retail herb houses may sell ganja to customers with a medical prescription or recommendation, up to two ounces at a time, and may let them consume it on site, a 2016 Gleaner column on the licensing rules explains. Since 2020, herb houses can take online orders from registered customers for pickup at a licensed outlet, and 2025 amendments to the licensing rules let retailers deliver.
buying.citation: Jamaica Gleaner, Aug 16 2016 (column); Ministry of Industry, Investment and Commerce, May 21 2020; Jamaica Information Service, Apr 17 2026

possession.short: Two ounces or less: a J$500 ticket
possession.detail: Having two ounces (about 57 grams) or less is not an arrestable offence. Police can issue a J$500 ticket, payable at a tax office within 30 days. Not paying is an offence that sends you to Petty Sessions Court, where a conviction goes on your record. Anyone under 18, or an adult who appears dependent, is referred to the National Council on Drug Abuse for counselling. More than two ounces is still a crime that can bring a fine, prison or both.
possession.citation: Ministry of Justice, Fact sheet on the Dangerous Drugs (Amendment) Act 2015

home-grow.short: Five plants per household
home-grow.detail: Each household may grow up to five ganja plants on its premises. Where several households share one property, each may grow five. Rastafarians 18 and older, and Rastafarian organisations, can apply for authorisation to grow it for sacramental use, but that ganja may not be sold or exported.
home-grow.citation: Ministry of Justice, Fact sheet on the Dangerous Drugs (Amendment) Act 2015

driving.short: No driving under the influence; up to J$50,000
driving.detail: The Road Traffic Act 2018, in force since February 1, 2023, makes it an offence to drive or be in charge of a vehicle while under the influence of alcohol or other drugs to the point of being unable to control it properly. A first conviction can bring a fine of up to J$50,000 and a 12-month driving ban unless the court finds special reasons. The Act sets no THC limit. It also lists smoking ganja while driving as a separate offence.
driving.citation: Road Traffic Act 2018 s. 66 and Fifth Schedule; Monitor Tribune, Feb 2023 (news)

record-relief.short: Small ganja convictions leave no record
record-relief.detail: A 2014 amendment to the Criminal Records (Rehabilitation of Offenders) Act provides that convictions for possessing two ounces or less, for smoking ganja, or for having a pipe or other smoking utensil do not go on a criminal record. A lawyer's advice column says people whose old conviction still shows can apply in writing to the Criminal Records (Rehabilitation of Offenders) Board.
record-relief.citation: Jamaica Information Service, Jul 7 2014; Jamaica Observer advice column, May 6 2018

border.short: No. Exporting is a serious crime
border.detail: The 2015 reform did not legalise taking ganja out of Jamaica, and the government says it significantly raised the penalties for exporting. Even ganja grown under a Rastafarian authorisation may not be exported. Importing is allowed only in narrow cases: patients with cancer or another serious illness certified by a doctor may import ganja-based medicine, and approved research bodies may import it for study, under the regulations.
border.citation: Ministry of Justice, Fact sheet on the Dangerous Drugs (Amendment) Act 2015

differences.title: What is different about Jamaica
points: Two ounces or less is handled like a traffic ticket: J$500, no arrest and no criminal record, as long as you pay within 30 days.
Rastafarian sacramental use is written into the law, including registered places of worship and events declared exempt.
The home-grow limit of five plants applies to each household, so several households on one property may each grow five.
Visitors can apply for a permit to buy up to two ounces for medical use on a home doctor's recommendation or their own signed declaration.
Herb houses can let customers smoke on site, which is otherwise banned in public and within five metres of a public place.
Convictions for small amounts, smoking and pipes are kept off criminal records under a 2014 change.
There is no THC limit for drivers; the test is whether you could properly control the vehicle.

CO.name: Colombia
CO.summary: Carrying a personal dose, 20 grams of marijuana, has not been a crime since a 1994 court ruling, and the law allows up to 20 plants. There is no legal adult market: two attempts to legalise one failed in the Senate in 2023. Medical cannabis is licensed, and dried flower became a medical product in October 2025.
CO.note: Spanish sources are summarized in English. Court rulings shape much of this law.

adult-use.short: Personal use is not a crime, but not legal either
adult-use.detail: In ruling C-221 of May 5, 1994, the Constitutional Court struck down the penalties for carrying and using a personal dose, holding that they violated personal autonomy. A 2009 constitutional amendment then banned carrying and using drugs except on prescription, but without criminal penalties; it allows only educational, preventive or therapeutic measures, with the person's consent. Using in parks and some public areas can be restricted by local rules.
adult-use.citation: Dejusticia, May 2024 (organization); Constitutional Court ruling C-127 of 2023 (communiqué)

medical.short: Yes, licensed, now including dried flower
medical.detail: Medical cannabis is regulated under Law 1787 of 2016 and its decrees. Decree 1138 of October 27, 2025 lets dried flower be sold and dispensed as a finished product for medical purposes only. Products above a THC limit set by the Ministry of Health are controlled and sold through pharmacies, and only pharmacies certified by the medicines regulator, INVIMA, may make up cannabis preparations. A trade publication reported that patients would get flower treatments under prescription and sanitary control.
medical.citation: Decreto 1138 de 2025; ConsultorSalud, Oct 29 2025 (news)

buying.short: No adult shops. Medical products through pharmacies
buying.detail: No law allows selling cannabis to adults for recreational use. A constitutional reform to create a regulated market fell short in its eighth and final Senate vote on June 20, 2023, 47 to 43 when 54 votes were needed, and a second attempt was shelved by the Senate, 46 to 40, on December 12, 2023. Medical products are sold through pharmacies.
buying.citation: Blu Radio, Jun 20 2023; Noticias RCN, Dec 12 2023; Decreto 1138 de 2025

possession.short: 20 grams is the personal dose, but intent is what counts
possession.detail: The 1986 drug law sets the personal dose at 20 grams of marijuana and 5 grams of hashish. Those figures are no longer the line: the Supreme Court has held that buying a larger supply for several occasions is not a crime, and that whatever the amount, prosecutors must prove intent to sell or distribute. In 2023 the Constitutional Court ruled that carrying a personal or medical dose cannot be punished under the rules on public spaces. Police still issued 1,188,906 tickets for possession and use in public space between 2017 and 2022, Dejusticia reports, and 99.6% of marijuana seizures were under 20 grams.
possession.citation: Dejusticia, May 2024 (organization); Constitutional Court ruling C-127 of 2023 (communiqué)

sharing.short: Sharing for free is not a crime; selling is
sharing.detail: In 2023 the Supreme Court recognised a "shared dose": carrying drugs to share for free with people you trust is not a crime. Selling, or carrying with intent to sell, remains drug trafficking.

home-grow.short: Up to 20 plants
home-grow.detail: Since the 1986 drug law, growing up to 20 plants from which a psychoactive substance can be extracted has not counted as a plantation. Decree 1138 of 2025 keeps home growing outside the medical licensing system, but home growers may not sell, give or deliver seeds, plants or cannabis products to anyone else.
home-grow.citation: Dejusticia, May 2024 (organization); Decreto 1138 de 2025

driving.short: Illegal; refusing a test means losing your licence
driving.detail: Law 1696 of 2013 makes driving under the effects of psychoactive substances an infraction punished with the fines in article 152 of the traffic code. That article grades penalties only by blood alcohol, so the text does not say which tier applies to cannabis alone. A driver who refuses the physical or clinical tests, or flees, has their licence cancelled, faces a fine of 1,440 daily minimum wages and has the vehicle impounded for 20 working days.
driving.citation: Ley 1696 de 2013, art. 131 lit. F and art. 152

experiment.text: Cities set their own rules on where you may use cannabis outdoors. The 2023 court ruling let mayors restrict consumption in parks and set zones to protect children, but not ban carrying a personal or medical dose, and it ordered a national protocol. Dejusticia reviewed 42 local decrees and counted at least 18 that ban possession outright and at least 10 that restrict use around the clock across nearly all public space.

differences.title: What is different about Colombia
points: Judges, not lawmakers, decriminalised personal use, in a 1994 ruling grounded in personal autonomy.
The Constitution itself bans carrying and using drugs without a prescription, yet forbids criminal punishment for it.
The 20-gram personal dose is a guide, not a ceiling: what makes it a crime is proof of intent to sell.
Growing up to 20 plants has been allowed since 1986, decades before the medical program existed.
Legalising a market needs a constitutional amendment and eight votes in Congress. The 2023 attempt won a majority in the Senate but not the 54 votes required.
Since October 2025 dried flower can be sold for medical use, with small and medium growers given priority for the domestic market.
Where you may smoke outdoors depends on your city, and many local rules go further than the courts allow.

IE.name: Ireland
IE.summary: Illegal for recreational use. Since December 2020 gardaí can caution a first-time adult found with cannabis for personal use instead of prosecuting. Specialist doctors can prescribe it for three conditions, and a 2026 Oireachtas committee called for decriminalising personal possession.
IE.note: Gardaí are the Irish police. The 1977 Act states its fines in Irish pounds; euro figures are the conversions noted in the Law Reform Commission's revised text.

adult-use.short: No. Possession is a crime
adult-use.detail: Possessing a controlled drug without authorisation is an offence under section 3 of the Misuse of Drugs Act 1977, and cannabis is controlled. A Citizens' Assembly recommended a health-led response in January 2024, and in June 2026 the Joint Committee on Drugs Use recommended repealing section 3 and fully decriminalising possession for personal use. An Irish Times editorial in July 2026 said government signals suggested little appetite for the change.
adult-use.citation: Misuse of Drugs Act 1977 (revised); Law Society Gazette, Jun 24 2026; Irish Times, Jul 2 2026 (editorial)

medical.short: Consultants only, for three conditions
medical.detail: Under the Medical Cannabis Access Programme, medical consultants can prescribe specified cannabis-based products to patients who have exhausted other treatments for spasticity in multiple sclerosis, nausea and vomiting from chemotherapy, or severe treatment-resistant epilepsy. For other conditions a doctor can apply to the Minister for Health for a licence for a named patient. A GP cannot prescribe on their own. The HSE reimburses only treatment for the three listed conditions.
medical.citation: Houses of the Oireachtas, Apr 19 2023; HSE, Medical Cannabis Products Reimbursement Scheme

buying.short: No legal sale except by prescription
buying.detail: There is no legal market for adults. Patients get products only on a consultant's prescription, and the HSE reimbursement scheme for the licence route covers products bought from one pharmacy in the Netherlands, Transvaal Apotheek.
buying.citation: Misuse of Drugs Act 1977 (revised); HSE, Medical Cannabis Products Reimbursement Scheme

possession.short: A first offence may get a caution; fines in court
possession.detail: Since December 14, 2020 gardaí can give an adult caution instead of prosecuting someone found with cannabis for personal use, for a first offence only and for no other drug. In court, the Act sets a maximum fine for personal-use possession of £300 (€380.92) on summary conviction for a first offence and £400 (€507.90) for a second. A third or later offence can bring up to 12 months in prison on summary conviction, or three years on indictment. The Irish Times reports that gardaí tend to prosecute only repeat offenders.
possession.citation: Misuse of Drugs Act 1977 s. 27 (revised); Offaly Express, Sep 2025 (news); Irish Times, Jul 2 2026

home-grow.short: No. Up to 14 years on indictment
home-grow.detail: Section 17 bans cultivating any plant of the genus Cannabis without a licence. The maximum penalty is 12 months in prison on summary conviction, or up to 14 years on indictment.
home-grow.citation: Misuse of Drugs Act 1977 ss. 17 and 27 (revised)

driving.short: 1 ng/ml of THC in blood, minimum 1-year ban
driving.detail: Under the Road Traffic Act 2016 it is an offence to drive with 1 nanogram of THC per millilitre of blood or more, or 5 ng/ml of its metabolite, whether or not you are impaired. Gardaí can test saliva at the roadside. Driving over the limit brings a disqualification of at least one year for a first offence and two years for a second. Driving while impaired brings at least four and six years. Fines run up to €5,000, with up to six months in prison on summary conviction. A medical exemption certificate covers prescribed cannabinoid products, but not driving while impaired.
driving.citation: Road Traffic Act 2016 s. 8; Garda Síochána, Preliminary Drug Testing FAQ (Dec 2022)

record-relief.short: A single minor conviction becomes spent after 7 years
record-relief.detail: Under the Criminal Justice (Spent Convictions and Certain Disclosures) Act 2016, a person with one, and only one, conviction that led to a fine or a prison term under 12 months no longer has to disclose it after seven years. There is no cannabis-specific expungement, and the government has said it is reviewing the Act with a view to widening it.

experiment.text: Ireland ran a Citizens' Assembly on Drugs Use from April to October 2023. Its final report made 36 recommendations. The closest vote was on cannabis: 39 members backed a health-led approach and 38 backed legalising and regulating cannabis.

differences.title: What is different about Ireland
points: Cannabis is the only drug covered by the adult caution: other drugs still go to court.
The law punishes cannabis possession for personal use with fines only for the first two offences; prison becomes possible from the third.
Medical cannabis exists, but only consultants can prescribe it and reimbursement covers just three conditions.
The drug-driving limit for THC is 1 ng/ml of blood, and an offence does not need proof of impairment.
A citizens' assembly came within one vote, 39 to 38, of backing a legal cannabis market over a health-led approach.
An Oireachtas committee recommended full decriminalisation of personal possession in June 2026; the government had not adopted it.

LU.name: Luxembourg
LU.summary: Since July 2023 adults may grow up to four plants per household from seed and use cannabis at home. There is no legal shop, and carrying it in public is still an offence, fined for 3 grams or less. Medical cannabis is free from hospital pharmacies for qualifying residents.
LU.note: French-language law texts are summarized in English.

adult-use.short: Yes, at home, from your own plants
adult-use.detail: The law of July 10, 2023, published on July 17, 2023, lets adults consume and hold home-grown cannabis at their home or usual residence. Using it outside the home is still an offence, fined €25 to €500. Using it in front of minors, at school or at work can bring 8 days to 6 months in prison and a fine of €251 to €2,500.
adult-use.citation: Loi du 10 juillet 2023 (Mémorial A 408); Bonn & Schmitt, Jul 24 2023 (law firm)

medical.short: Yes, free from hospital pharmacies
medical.detail: Prescription has been allowed since July 2018. A doctor licensed in Luxembourg who has completed a training course certified by the Health Directorate can prescribe dried flower or oil with set THC and CBD levels for severe chronic pain that has not responded to treatment, nausea from chemotherapy, or spasticity in multiple sclerosis. It is dispensed free of charge at four hospital pharmacies, within 60 days of the prescription. Patients must live in Luxembourg, be covered by its health insurance or hold Luxembourg nationality.
medical.citation: Health Directorate, How to access medicinal cannabis

buying.detail: The 2023 law legalised growing at home, not selling. Acquiring cannabis is still an offence: up to 3 grams brings a fine, and more than 3 grams can bring 8 days to 6 months in prison and a fine of up to €2,500. Medical cannabis comes only from hospital pharmacies.
buying.citation: Loi du 10 juillet 2023; Health Directorate, How to access medicinal cannabis

possession.short: At home, no set limit; in public, 3 grams means a fine
possession.detail: At home adults may hold what they grow. In public, possessing or transporting 3 grams or less is a minor offence with a fine of €25 to €500, and police or customs can issue a €145 on-the-spot notice instead; if it is paid within 45 days, prosecution ends. More than 3 grams is a criminal offence punishable by 8 days to 6 months in prison and a fine of €251 to €2,500.
possession.citation: Loi du 10 juillet 2023 arts. 7-1 and 7-3

sharing.short: No. Only home use is legal
sharing.detail: The law allows holding and using home-grown cannabis at home, not passing it on. Offering cannabis to a minor, home-grown included, can bring 6 months to 2 years in prison and a fine of up to €25,000, and providing premises or means for others to use it is a separate offence.

home-grow.short: Four plants per household, from seed
home-grow.detail: Up to four plants per household, meaning everyone who shares a home and a common budget, not per person. Only an adult may grow them, only from seed, at the home or usual residence, and they must not be visible from the public road. More plants, or growing somewhere else, can bring 8 days to 5 years in prison and a fine of €500 to €250,000.
home-grow.citation: Loi du 10 juillet 2023 arts. 7-1 and 7-2; Bonn & Schmitt (law firm)

driving.short: 1 ng/ml of THC in blood serum
driving.detail: Driving with a THC level of 1 nanogram per millilitre of blood serum or more is an offence under article 12 of the road traffic law of February 14, 1955. It carries 8 days to 3 years in prison, a fine of €500 to €10,000, or both, and courts can ban the driver for 3 months to 15 years, as a 2024 criminal judgment sets out.
driving.citation: Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg, judgment of Mar 14 2024

differences.title: What is different about Luxembourg
points: The four-plant limit is per household with a shared budget, so three adults living together still share four plants.
Plants must start from seed and must not be visible from the public road.
Home growing is legal, but there is nowhere to buy cannabis legally, so seeds are the only lawful starting point.
Carrying up to 3 grams in public can end with a €145 notice paid on the spot instead of a court case.
Medical cannabis is dispensed free of charge, but only to residents, people insured in Luxembourg or Luxembourg nationals.
Legal home use does not change the road rules: 1 ng/ml of THC in blood serum is an offence.

BE.name: Belgium
BE.summary: Illegal, but tolerated in small amounts. Since 2005 an adult with up to 3 grams or one plant and no aggravating circumstances is the lowest prosecution priority. Medical use is limited to approved medicines such as Sativex and prescribed CBD preparations. Drivers face zero tolerance.
BE.note: French-language sources are summarized in English. Belgium's regions run their own road safety agencies.

adult-use.short: No. Small amounts are the lowest priority
adult-use.detail: Cannabis is illegal under the drug law of February 24, 1921. A joint directive of the Minister of Justice and the prosecutors general from 2005 puts possession of up to 3 grams, or one plant grown for personal use, by an adult at the lowest level of prosecution priority. The tolerance does not apply where there are aggravating circumstances or a disturbance of public order. For anyone under 18, using and possessing cannabis are prohibited.
adult-use.citation: Province de Liège, Le cannabis et la loi; EMCDDA Country Drug Report 2017

medical.short: Approved medicines and CBD preparations only
medical.detail: A Royal Decree of June 2015 allowed THC-containing medicines to be prescribed. Pharmacists can dispense authorised cannabis-based medicines such as Sativex on prescription, and prepare CBD preparations for a patient on a doctor's prescription if THC exposure stays very low. A 2019 law created a state cannabis agency to supply medicinal cannabis, but it was not yet active as of April 2021.
medical.citation: EMCDDA Country Drug Report 2017; CMS expert guide (updated Apr 2021, law firm)

buying.detail: Selling cannabis is trafficking, an aggravating circumstance that takes a case outside the tolerance. Producing, importing and selling recreational cannabis is prohibited.
buying.citation: Province de Liège, Le cannabis et la loi; CMS expert guide (law firm)

possession.short: 3 grams: a simplified report and a fine
possession.detail: For an adult with up to 3 grams and no aggravating circumstances, police write a simplified report and do not seize the cannabis, and the report goes to the prosecutor once a month. The CMS guide puts the fine at €120 to €200. The tolerance ends with possession in a school or near one, in a prison, conspicuous possession in public, driving, or a minor being present. Aggravated cases can bring 3 months to 1 year in prison and a heavy fine.
possession.citation: Province de Liège, Le cannabis et la loi; CMS expert guide (law firm); EMCDDA 2017

home-grow.short: One plant is tolerated, not legal
home-grow.detail: Growing remains illegal, but one plant grown for personal use by an adult falls within the lowest prosecution priority, and in principle will not be prosecuted.
home-grow.citation: Province de Liège, Le cannabis et la loi; CMS expert guide (law firm)

driving.short: Zero tolerance; licence withdrawn on the spot
driving.detail: Driving under the influence of any drug is prohibited under zero tolerance. If a roadside saliva test finds THC, police withdraw the licence immediately, for at least 15 days and up to six and a half months, and the case goes to the police court. The court can fine a first offender €1,600 to €16,000 and ban them from driving for 1 month to 5 years or for good; repeat offenders face €3,200 to €40,000. THC can show up in saliva 14 hours or more after use, and drivers involved in an accident are tested as a matter of course.
driving.citation: Brussels-Capital Region, Alcool, drogues, médicaments au volant; AWSR leaflet (May 2026)

differences.title: What is different about Belgium
points: The tolerance comes from a prosecutors' directive, not from a change to the 1921 law.
Police do not seize 3 grams or less from an adult when the tolerance applies; they write a simplified report.
Being near a school, carrying cannabis openly in public or having a minor present is enough to lose the tolerance.
There is no medical flower program: patients get approved medicines or prescribed CBD preparations.
A positive saliva test means losing your licence on the spot for at least 15 days, even before any court hearing.

FR.name: France
FR.summary: Illegal, with no distinction between cannabis and other drugs. Police can settle simple use of cannabis by an adult with a €200 on-the-spot criminal fine. A medical cannabis experiment closed to new patients at the end of 2024 while the government prepares to make it permanent.
FR.note: French sources are summarized in English.

adult-use.short: No. Use is a crime
adult-use.detail: Illicit use of any drug classified as a narcotic is punishable by one year in prison and a €3,750 fine under article L.3421-1 of the Public Health Code. The law makes no distinction between cannabis and other drugs.
adult-use.citation: Drogues Info Service, L'usage de stupéfiants (May 2026)

medical.short: An experiment, closed to new patients
medical.detail: An experiment run by the medicines agency ANSM let trained doctors prescribe medical cannabis in a few indications, mostly refractory nerve pain, along with epilepsy, multiple sclerosis spasticity, cancer symptoms and palliative care. New patients could no longer join after the end of 2024. Patients still treated on December 31, 2024 keep receiving treatment beyond March 31, 2026 by ministerial decision, and ANSM counted roughly 700 of them in early 2026. The 2024 social security financing law provides for making medical cannabis permanent; the decrees to do so were still awaited in spring 2026.
medical.citation: ANSM committee minutes, Jan 14 2026; Le Quotidien du Pharmacien, Apr 9 2026 (news)

buying.detail: Buying, possessing, transporting and offering drugs are trafficking offences punishable by up to 10 years in prison and a €7.5 million fine. Selling or giving to someone for their personal use carries up to 5 years and €75,000.
buying.citation: Drogues Info Service, Le trafic de stupéfiants (May 2026)

possession.short: Small amounts: a €200 criminal fine
possession.detail: Since 2019 police can settle simple use by an adult with an on-the-spot criminal fine (amende forfaitaire délictuelle) of €200, cut to €150 if paid within 15 days and raised to €450 after 45 days. It is limited by ministry instructions to cannabis, cocaine and ecstasy, and excludes people already known to police for drug offences. Paying ends the case but counts as an admission and goes on the criminal record. A 2026 bill on public order would raise the fine to €500; an amendment filed in June 2026 sought to strike that increase, and we could not confirm the outcome.
possession.citation: Drogues Info Service, L'usage de stupéfiants (May 2026); Assemblée nationale amendment CL305

sharing.short: No. Sharing is treated as trafficking
sharing.detail: Sharing with friends, or buying for a group, is in legal terms a transfer and acquisition of drugs, Drogues Info Service warns, even when people see it as doing someone a favour.
sharing.citation: Drogues Info Service, Le trafic de stupéfiants (May 2026)

home-grow.short: No. Growing counts as production
home-grow.detail: Illicit production of drugs is a crime under article 222-35 of the Penal Code, punishable by 20 years and a €7.5 million fine. A 2013 Senate note observed that the law makes no separate provision for growing for personal use.
home-grow.citation: Drogues Info Service, Le trafic de stupéfiants; Sénat note LC 238 (2013)

driving.short: Any detected use: up to 3 years and €9,000
driving.detail: Driving after using drugs is an offence under article L235-1 of the Highway Code once a saliva or blood analysis confirms use; there is no THC threshold. Since July 11, 2025 the maximum is 3 years in prison and a €9,000 fine, and the driver automatically loses half the licence points, 6 out of 12. Police can hold the licence for 72 hours, the prefect can suspend it for up to a year, and a court can suspend it for up to 5 years or cancel it.
driving.citation: Drogues Info Service, La conduite automobile et les drogues (Feb 2026); Legipermis

differences.title: What is different about France
points: French drug law treats cannabis exactly like heroin or cocaine: there is no lower category for it.
The €200 on-the-spot fine is a criminal penalty, not a ticket: paying it puts the offence on your record.
Sharing a joint with friends counts legally as transferring drugs, a trafficking offence.
There is no THC limit for drivers. Any use confirmed by a saliva or blood test is enough.
Medical cannabis exists only as an experiment that stopped taking new patients at the end of 2024; about 700 patients still receive it.

IT.name: Italy
IT.summary: Possession for personal use is not a crime but brings administrative penalties, such as losing your driving licence or passport for a few months. Italy's highest court has held that growing a few plants at home for yourself is not a crime. Doctors can prescribe medical cannabis, including flower grown by a military pharmaceutical plant.
IT.note: Italian sources are summarized in English.

adult-use.short: Not a crime, but punished administratively
adult-use.detail: Possession is never allowed by Italian law, a prefecture FAQ stresses. If the amount is small and nothing suggests sale or giving it to others, it is treated as personal use and reported to the Prefect, who can impose administrative penalties under article 75 of the 1990 drug law.
adult-use.citation: Prefettura, FAQ on article 75 DPR 309/1990

medical.short: Yes, any doctor can prescribe it
medical.detail: Any licensed doctor can prescribe cannabis flower as a magistral preparation on a non-repeatable prescription, with the patient's written informed consent, when standard treatments have failed. Listed uses include chronic and neuropathic pain, spasticity in multiple sclerosis, nausea from chemotherapy, appetite loss, glaucoma and Tourette syndrome. Italy's own flower, Cannabis FM2, is grown by the military pharmaceutical plant in Florence and has been available since December 2016. It is taken as a tea or with a vaporiser, and smoking is advised against. Whether the health service pays depends on the region.
medical.citation: Ministry of Health and Defence working group, FM2 prescriber recommendations (Feb 2017)

buying.detail: There is no legal adult market. Selling, offering or giving cannabis to others takes a case outside personal use. Patients get prescribed flower as a pharmacy preparation.
buying.citation: Prefettura FAQ; FM2 prescriber recommendations (Feb 2017)

possession.short: Personal use: 1 to 3 months without a licence or passport
possession.detail: For cannabis, the Prefect can suspend or bar a driving licence, gun permit, passport or ID card valid for travel for one to three months; for other drugs it is two months to a year. On a first report the case can end with a formal warning if the person attends an interview, and completing an agreed treatment or education programme entitles the person to have the measure lifted. Police can also take a driver's licence for 30 days on the spot. Reports stay in the prefecture's files with no expiry.
possession.citation: Prefettura, FAQ on article 75 DPR 309/1990

sharing.short: No. Giving it away is not personal use
sharing.detail: Personal use covers only someone's own consumption. Selling, offering or giving cannabis to anyone else falls outside it.

home-grow.short: A few plants at home is not a crime, per the top court
home-grow.detail: In ruling 12348 of 2020 the joint sections of the Court of Cassation held that very small domestic cultivation falls outside the criminal offence when the techniques are rudimentary, the plants few, the yield very modest, and nothing points to the drug market. The cannabis produced still counts as possession for personal use, so the administrative penalties can apply. Larger grows remain a crime.
home-grow.citation: Studio Cataldi on Cassazione SU n. 12348/2020 (legal news)

driving.short: Up to €6,000, arrest and a 1-2 year suspension
driving.detail: Since December 14, 2024, article 187 of the Highway Code punishes driving after taking drugs, no longer requiring proof of impairment. Penalties are a fine of €1,500 to €6,000, arrest of six months to a year and a licence suspension of one to two years, doubled if the driver does not own the vehicle. In January 2026 the Constitutional Court upheld the law but read it narrowly: prosecutors must show the substance was taken close enough to driving that it could still impair an average user.
driving.citation: Pagella Politica, Dec 13 2024 (news); Corte costituzionale, sentenza 10/2026

differences.title: What is different about Italy
points: Personal use is punished by taking away documents, not by fines or prison: a driving licence or passport can be suspended.
The penalties are lighter for cannabis than for other drugs: one to three months instead of up to a year.
Courts, not lawmakers, carved out home growing: a few plants grown with rudimentary means for yourself is not a crime.
The state grows its own medical cannabis at a military pharmaceutical plant in Florence.
A 2024 law dropped the need to prove impairment for drug driving, but the Constitutional Court still requires use close to the time of driving.

AT.name: Austria
AT.summary: Illegal, but when cannabis was only for personal use, the drug law requires prosecutors to set the case aside on probation. Doctors can prescribe cannabinoid medicines such as dronabinol, but not cannabis flower.
AT.note: German-language sources are summarized in English.

adult-use.short: No. Possession is a crime under the drug law
adult-use.detail: Acquiring and possessing cannabis are offences under § 27 of the Narcotic Substances Act (Suchtmittelgesetz). Section 35 then steers personal-use cases away from court.
adult-use.citation: Suchtmittelgesetz § 35 (RIS)

medical.short: Cannabinoid medicines, not flower
medical.detail: Dronabinol, Sativex and Epidiolex can be prescribed under certain conditions, a medical portal notes. Cannabis flower is not prescribed: in 2019 the Supreme Health Council found no scientific evidence to support it, and the National Council took note of that report.
medical.citation: praktischArzt.at (medical portal); Tiroler Tageszeitung/APA, Mar 27 2019 (news)

possession.short: Personal use: case set aside on 1-2 years' probation
possession.detail: When the offence was committed only for the accused's own or another person's personal use and they gained no advantage, the public prosecutor must provisionally withdraw from prosecution and set a probation period of one to two years. Normally a health authority must first say whether a health measure is needed, but for cannabis the prosecutor can skip that statement, unless there was a drug investigation against the person in the previous five years.
possession.citation: Suchtmittelgesetz § 35 (RIS)

sharing.short: Passing it on without profit is diverted like personal use
sharing.detail: The personal-use rule covers using drugs for another person's personal use as long as the accused gained no advantage, and for cannabis it covers passing it to someone for their own use. Selling remains trafficking.

home-grow.short: No, but personal-use growing is diverted
home-grow.detail: Growing cannabis to obtain the drug is an offence. Where it was only for personal use, the same provisional withdrawal from prosecution applies, and the prosecutor can again skip the health authority's statement.
home-grow.citation: Suchtmittelgesetz § 35(4) (RIS)

driving.short: No limit value; a doctor decides impairment
driving.detail: Anyone whose consciousness is impaired by a drug may not drive. There is no limit value as there is for alcohol: police use a checklist and a saliva pre-test, then an authorised doctor examines the driver and takes blood if impairment is confirmed. Penalties equal those for alcohol at 0.4 to 0.59 mg/l of breath. Refusing the test can be penalised, and the examination costs are charged only if impairment is found.
driving.citation: oesterreich.gv.at, Drogen am Steuer (Jan 2026)

differences.title: What is different about Austria
points: The law does not just allow leniency for personal use: prosecutors must provisionally drop such cases, with one to two years of probation.
Passing cannabis to someone for their own use, with no profit, is handled under the same personal-use rule.
There is no THC limit for drivers. A doctor's examination of actual impairment decides the case.
Cannabis medicines are available, but flower is not, after a 2019 health council report found no evidence for it.

DK.name: Denmark
DK.summary: Illegal. Possession for your own use is normally a fine, starting at 2,000 kroner for under 10 grams. Fines double in designated penalty zones. Medical cannabis, including dried flower, has been prescribed since 2018, and the scheme became permanent on January 1, 2026.
DK.note: Danish sources are summarized in English. Amounts are in Danish kroner (DKK).

adult-use.short: No. Possession is an offence
adult-use.detail: Breaking the Act on Euphoriant Substances is punishable by a fine or up to two years in prison. Possession for your own use is, as a clear rule, punished with a fine from the prosecutors' standard table, and the cannabis is confiscated.
adult-use.citation: Rigsadvokatmeddelelsen om narkotika (Apr 2026); Lovguiden

medical.short: Yes, prescribed and sold by pharmacies
medical.detail: A trial began on January 1, 2018 and was made permanent from January 1, 2026. Any doctor can prescribe for pain; for multiple sclerosis, spinal cord injury or chemotherapy nausea the guidance points to the relevant specialist. Products include dried flower, oil and capsules, dispensed by pharmacies on an electronic prescription covering at most a month. The state subsidy covers 50% of the first 20,000 kroner a year, so at most 10,000 kroner. Patients prove lawful possession with the prescription, the pharmacy-labelled pack and the receipt.
medical.citation: Lovguiden, Medicinsk cannabis (compilation)

possession.short: Under 10 grams: a 2,000-kroner fine
possession.detail: Up to about 10 grams of hash or cannabis is presumed to be for your own use. Fines for a first offence are 2,000 kroner under 10 grams, 3,000 from 10 to 49.9 grams and 5,000 from 50 to 99.9 grams; they rise by half for a second offence and double from the third. From 100 grams the starting point is prison. Fines are lower for under-18s and people on very low incomes. In designated penalty zones the fine is doubled, and a repeat offence there normally means prison.
possession.citation: Rigsadvokatmeddelelsen om narkotika (Apr 2026)

sharing.short: No. Selling small amounts doubles the fine
sharing.detail: Selling under 50 grams of hash can be fined for a first offence, generally at double the possession fine, but organised selling, such as through known sales points or phone-order couriers, can mean prison even the first time. Patients may not share their medical cannabis.
sharing.citation: Rigsadvokatmeddelelsen om narkotika (Apr 2026); Lovguiden, Medicinsk cannabis

home-grow.short: No. Plants are fined by weight
home-grow.detail: Cannabis plants are treated as a separate category in the fine table: a first offence costs 2,000 kroner for under 99.9 grams of plant material, 3,000 for 100 to 249.9 grams and 5,000 for 250 to 999.9 grams. The own-use guideline for plants is 100 grams.
home-grow.citation: Lovguiden, fine table under § 3 of the Act on Euphoriant Substances

driving.short: Zero tolerance: 0.001 mg THC per kg of blood
driving.detail: It is an offence to drive with more than 0.001 milligrams of THC per kilogram of blood, unless it was taken under a lawful prescription. Even then, a patient who is unfit to drive can be prosecuted, and official guidance recommends that doctors ban patients in the medical scheme from driving for the whole treatment period.
driving.citation: Lovguiden, Medicinsk cannabis and færdselsloven § 54

differences.title: What is different about Denmark
points: Prosecutors publish a fixed fine table, so the fine depends on the weight and on how many times you have been caught.
Police can designate penalty zones where fines are doubled; a case over 117 grams of hash in Christiania's Pusher Street went to the top courts on how that doubling works.
Medical patients can get dried flower from pharmacies, but the subsidy stops at 10,000 kroner a year.
The THC driving limit is effectively zero, and patients are usually told not to drive at all during treatment.

BR.name: Brazil
BR.summary: Since a June 2024 Supreme Court ruling, carrying up to 40 grams or growing up to six female plants for your own use is no longer a crime, but cannabis is still prohibited: police seize it and a judge can order a warning or an educational course. There is no legal adult market. Medical products are sold in pharmacies on prescription or imported with approval from Anvisa, the health regulator.
BR.note: Portuguese sources are summarized in English. Court rulings shape much of this law.

adult-use.short: Not a crime since 2024, but still prohibited
adult-use.detail: In June 2024 the Supreme Federal Court (STF) ruled in RE 635659 (Tema 506) that acquiring, keeping, transporting or carrying cannabis for personal consumption is not a criminal offence. It stays an unlawful act outside criminal law: police seize the cannabis, and a judge can impose a warning about its effects and attendance at an educational programme, in a non-criminal procedure. The ruling covers cannabis only, and there is no legal place to buy it for adult use.
adult-use.citation: STF, RE 635659 (Tema 506), thesis fixed Jun 26 2024; TJMG summary of the thesis

medical.short: Pharmacy products on prescription, or import
medical.detail: Anvisa rule RDC 1.015/2026 replaced RDC 327/2019 and took effect on May 4, 2026. Authorised cannabis products are dispensed by a pharmacist in pharmacies and drugstores. Doctors and dentists can prescribe them when no registered medicine is a satisfactory alternative. Products with up to 0.2% THC need a special control prescription; above 0.2% THC needs a Notificação de Receita A, and those products are limited to serious debilitating or life-threatening conditions. The 2026 rule named fibromyalgia and lupus among the qualifying conditions and added skin, under-the-tongue, cheek and inhaled forms. Separately, a patient can apply to Anvisa to import a product for personal use under RDC 660/2022.
medical.citation: Anvisa, Q&A on RDC 1.015/2026 (Jul 20 2026), arts. 5, 35-37; Anvisa (Feb 3 2026); CFF (Mar 9 2026)

buying.detail: There is no legal adult-use sale. Selling, supplying or delivering drugs, even for free, is trafficking under article 33 of the Drug Law, punished with 5 to 15 years in prison and a fine. Buying for your own use falls under the Supreme Court's non-criminal treatment, but the cannabis is still seized. The legal purchase is a prescribed product from a pharmacy or drugstore.
buying.citation: Lei 11.343/2006 art. 33; STF Tema 506; Anvisa RDC 1.015/2026 Q&A

possession.short: Up to 40 grams is presumed personal use
possession.detail: Until Congress legislates, anyone with up to 40 grams of cannabis or six female plants is presumed to be a user. The presumption is relative: police can still arrest for trafficking below that amount if there are signs of sale, such as packaging, scales or sales records, but the police chief must justify it in detail and a judge reviews it at the custody hearing. Above 40 grams, a judge can still find personal use if there is enough proof. The sanctions are a warning and an educational programme, with no criminal consequences.
possession.citation: STF, RE 635659 (Tema 506), thesis items 1-8; STF news (Jun 26 2024)

sharing.detail: Offering cannabis occasionally and without profit to someone you know, so you can use it together, is a crime under article 33, paragraph 3 of the Drug Law: 6 months to 1 year of detention plus a fine. Other supplying, even for free, is trafficking under article 33. The 2024 ruling addresses possession for personal consumption.

home-grow.short: Six female plants presumed personal; medical growers go to court
home-grow.detail: The Drug Law treats growing a small amount for your own use the same way as possession (article 28, paragraph 1), and the Supreme Court's presumption covers six female plants, so this is handled outside criminal law but is not legal. Patients who grow for treatment have won habeas corpus orders (salvo-conduto) from the Superior Court of Justice case by case, with proof of medical need; the order is limited to the prescription and bars selling or giving away the plants or extracts. Anvisa's February 2026 rules authorise production only by companies after inspection, plus a separate route for nonprofit patient associations that does not allow commercial sale.
home-grow.citation: Lei 11.343/2006 art. 28 §1; STF Tema 506; STJ (Jun 7 2023); Anvisa (Feb 3 2026)

driving.short: Driving under the influence is banned
driving.detail: Under article 165 of the Traffic Code, driving under the influence of alcohol or any other psychoactive substance that causes dependence is a very serious violation: a fine of ten times the base amount, a 12-month suspension, the licence taken and the vehicle held. Impairment can be shown by a blood test, a clinical exam or a set of observed signs. Driving with impaired capacity is also a crime under article 306, with 6 months to 3 years of detention. The 2024 ruling did not change these rules.
driving.citation: Código de Trânsito Brasileiro arts. 165 and 306; CONTRAN MBFT ficha 516-92; Vrum (news, Sep 2024)

record-relief.short: No criminal record for personal possession
record-relief.detail: The Supreme Court ruled that sanctions for personal possession are applied with no criminal repercussion. It also told the National Council of Justice, with the Public Defender's Office, to run prison reviews to correct arrests made outside the ruling's limits. No automatic clearing of older convictions was found in the sources reviewed.

border.short: Importing is trafficking; medical import needs Anvisa
border.detail: Importing or exporting drugs without authorisation is trafficking under article 33 of the Drug Law, with 5 to 15 years in prison, and the penalty rises by one sixth to two thirds when the crime crosses national borders (article 40, I). The route for an individual to bring in a cannabis product is an Anvisa authorisation under RDC 660/2022, for personal use with a prescription.
border.citation: Lei 11.343/2006 arts. 33 and 40, I; Anvisa RDC 1.015/2026 Q&A (on RDC 660/2022)

experiment.text: Anvisa's 2026 update opens a possible path for compounding pharmacies to prepare cannabis products, but a specific rule still has to be written and approved before that can happen.

differences.title: What is different about Brazil
points: The change came from the Supreme Court, not Congress. The 40-gram line applies until Congress passes its own rule.
The 40 grams is a starting presumption, not a safe harbour: signs of sale can still lead to a trafficking arrest.
Patients who grow at home rely on individual court orders rather than a licence.
Nonprofit patient associations have their own route under Anvisa's 2026 rules, without commercial sale.

AR.name: Argentina
AR.summary: In the 2009 Arriola ruling the Supreme Court held that punishing an adult for possessing drugs for personal use, when it puts no one else at risk, is unconstitutional. Congress never changed the drug law, so possession is still written as a crime and courts decide case by case. Registered medical patients can grow up to nine flowering plants through the REPROCANN registry. There is no legal market.
AR.note: Spanish sources are summarized in English. Court rulings shape much of this law.

adult-use.short: Protected in private by a court ruling, not by law
adult-use.detail: On August 25, 2009, in the Arriola case, the Supreme Court found the personal-use possession offence in article 14 of Law 23.737 unconstitutional under article 19 of the Constitution, but only where possession for one's own use creates no concrete danger or harm to others. Courts apply that test case by case. The text of the law was not changed, and conspicuous use with public reach is still punishable under article 12.
adult-use.citation: CSJN, Arriola (Fallos 332:1963, Aug 25 2009), as applied by the Procuración General (Mar 5 2015); Ley 23.737 arts. 12, 14

medical.short: Registered patients can grow or have it grown
medical.detail: Law 27.350 (2017) set up medical cannabis access, and the Health Ministry's REPROCANN registry authorises patients with a medical indication to grow for themselves, through one third-party grower, or through a registered nonprofit association or foundation. Resolution 1780/2025 rewrote the rules: doctors must be registered and trained, a patient's permit lasts three years, and all access must be non-commercial. The consent form notes that home-made derivatives are not ANMAT-approved medicines.
medical.citation: Ministerio de Salud, Resolución 1780/2025 (Boletín Oficial May 23 2025), citing Ley 27.350

buying.detail: There is no legal adult-use market. Trading, distributing or holding drugs for sale carries 4 to 15 years in prison under article 5 of Law 23.737. REPROCANN access must be without commercial purpose, and producing or selling cannabis outside the permitted cases remains an offence under that law.
buying.citation: Ley 23.737 art. 5; Resolución 1780/2025

possession.short: Still a crime on paper; private use protected case by case
possession.detail: Article 14 of Law 23.737 still punishes possession with 1 to 6 years, or 1 month to 2 years when the small amount and circumstances clearly show personal use. Under Arriola, courts must not punish personal possession that creates no concrete danger or harm to others, judged case by case. Registered REPROCANN patients may carry up to 40 grams of dried flower or six 30 ml bottles of oil.
possession.citation: Ley 23.737 art. 14; CSJN Arriola (2009); Resolución 1780/2025 Annex II

sharing.short: Giving it away is a crime
sharing.detail: Supplying drugs free of charge carries 3 to 12 years under article 5 of Law 23.737. When the supply is occasional, free, small and clearly for the recipient's own use, the penalty drops to 6 months to 3 years. Promoting use or inducing someone to use carries 2 to 6 years under article 12.
sharing.citation: Ley 23.737 arts. 5 (inc. e and last paragraph) and 12

home-grow.short: Up to nine flowering plants with a REPROCANN permit
home-grow.detail: Registered patients may grow 1 to 9 flowering plants each, on up to 6 square metres indoors or 15 square metres outdoors. Without a permit, growing is a crime under article 5 of Law 23.737; when the small amount and circumstances clearly show personal use, the penalty is 1 month to 2 years.
home-grow.citation: Resolución 1780/2025 Annex II; Ley 23.737 art. 5

driving.short: No driving after drugs; zero alcohol
driving.detail: Since Law 27.714 (Boletín Oficial May 3 2023), article 48 of the national Traffic Law bans driving after consuming narcotics or medicines that reduce the ability to drive, and sets a zero blood-alcohol limit for every vehicle. Checks use a method approved by the health authority.
driving.citation: Ley 24.449 art. 48 a), as amended by Ley 27.714

record-relief.short: Treatment or education can replace a sentence
record-relief.detail: For personal-use cases, a judge can suspend the case or sentence and order treatment (articles 17 and 18), or, once, replace the penalty with an educational programme for a non-dependent first-time user (article 21). After three years of recovery, a judge may order the drug-use entry removed from the national criminal records registry (article 22).

experiment.text: A registered nonprofit association or foundation can grow for up to 150 REPROCANN patients, and a third-party grower can grow for themselves and one other patient. The 2025 rules tightened these roles after the Health Ministry said some growers were using them commercially.

differences.title: What is different about Argentina
points: Arriola changed how courts treat private possession, but the drug law still lists it as a crime.
Medical access runs through a national registry that lets patients grow, rather than only through pharmacies.
Associations and foundations can grow for registered patients, without selling.
Driving rules are strict: zero alcohol and no driving after drugs that reduce driving ability.

travel_warnings.detail: Possession of even very small quantities can lead to the death penalty, according to UK travel advice. Singapore classes cannabis as a Class A drug, with up to 10 years in prison and a fine of up to S$20,000 for consumption. Drug use detected on arrival can mean arrest.
Zero tolerance. Possessing, using, making or trafficking drugs can bring long prison sentences or the death penalty. Airports scan transit passengers' bags for cannabis.

Possession, trafficking and manufacture of any illegal drug, including cannabis, are serious offences. British travellers have been caught carrying cannabis while only transiting. Australia lists Malaysia among countries that apply the death penalty to drug offences.

Possession is a crime outside a COFEPRIS permit, and visitors have no permit. The U.S. government warns that drug possession and use, including medical marijuana, is illegal in Mexico and may result in a lengthy jail sentence.
UAE authorities treat drugs found in your bloodstream as possession, so use before arrival can lead to charges. Some CBD products are illegal.
Since December 12, 2024, using cannabis is a crime. Possession, use and transfer each carry up to 7 years in prison, and import carries 1 to 10 years.
Possession or use can bring up to 5 years in prison, and smuggling carries much longer terms, followed by deportation and an entry ban (Thai embassy warning).

travel_warnings.risk: Up to 10 years at the border
travel_warnings.detail: Since June 2026, bringing cannabis across Thailand's border can mean up to 10 years in prison, a fine of up to 500,000 baht, or both.
Australia's government lists these among countries that apply the death penalty to drug offences.

texas_concentrates.text: In Texas, THC concentrates (vape oil, wax, most edibles) are not treated as marijuana. They are Penalty Group 2 controlled substances, and possessing less than 1 gram is a state jail felony: 180 days to 2 years and a fine of up to $10,000.
